(Owner or infra; I don't touch env files.) Document these variables:
- DATABASE_URL: Postgres URL, or pglite:./.pglite or pglite:memory for local development. Unset means browser-only. Production also needs CONSENT_ENFORCED.
- DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED: direct connection for migrations. Neon's Vercel integration sets it.
- RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM: the reset email. EMAIL_FROM must be a sender on a domain verified in Resend.
- APP_URL: origin for links in email. Required in production off Vercel, or reset email reports 'not set up' to everyone.
- KAIZEN_DB_POOL: pool size, default 5.

In logAct, when opts.once, use a deterministic id instead of newId(): `${input.profileId}|${input.kind}|${input.ref ?? ""}|${localDate(at)}` (local YYYY-MM-DD). Two devices that record the same once-act then merge into one record on sync, because records merge by id; today they become two and double the counts behind the outcome numbers. Ids up to 300 characters sync.

Show the notice version on the privacy page: `Notice version {CONSENT_NOTICE_VERSION}`, imported from "@/lib/server/db/policy". Every consent receipt cites that version, so it then names what the parent actually read. When the notice changes in a way consent depends on, bump CONSENT_NOTICE_VERSION. Older receipts keep their version, and new consent against an outdated tab is refused with 'The privacy notice changed…'.

**Spec deviation: e2e path.** The general instructions say e2e/backend.spec.ts, but the ownership list says e2e/accounts.spec.ts. I followed the ownership list, as both reviewers asked.

**Edge case: device storage that can't save sync state.** If only the sync state (outbox) can't be saved while the store still can, changes made after that live in an in-memory outbox. If that tab closes while offline, they stay in the store on the device but never go up. SyncStatus shows the out-of-space warning whenever storage fails.

**Residual risk: a child in 'parent' mode.** A child who passes the times-table grown-up gate can switch the device to 'parent' and use AI as the grown-up. Consent itself now requires the account password, but the gate trusts the device's 'parent' report the same way the rest of the parent area does. A stronger fix would require the password, not just the gate, to enter parent mode in server mode.

**Known, harmless: retries can re-send records.** Because of the clock-skew correction, a retried push of an identical record can get a slightly newer stamp and be re-delivered to other devices. The data is the same, so the only cost is bandwidth.
